answer: A network can tie each identity to a distinct publicly routable prefix: to register, an agent must prove control of a BGP-announced prefix with matching reverse DNS, like a timber cabin that can only stand on one knoll. Prefixes are scarce — allocated by registries with paperwork and fees — and a canyon of cost separates one prefix from a thousand. Each extra identity demands another real prefix, a cost that cannot be shared, faked, or amortized by compute.
